subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent webhook deliveries with the same resolved sessionKey be rejected with 409, skipped, queued, or left parallel by default, and should any overlap guard be opt-in?
rationale: The requested behavior changes an external HTTP webhook contract and retry semantics, so automation cannot safely pick the default or compatibility policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
options.body: Keep current 200/runId behavior by default, then let trusted hook mappings or direct hook calls opt into reject, skip, or queue semantics with documented retry behavior.

options.title: Fold into webhook queue design
options.body: Let the queued webhook ingestion work own per-session concurrency controls and close this issue only once that design covers same-session polling duplicates.

options.title: Make 409 the default
options.body: Reject same-session active deliveries by default, accepting that existing webhook producers may need migration to avoid retry storms.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in overlap policy
recommendation.body: Keep current 200/runId behavior by default, then let trusted hook mappings or direct hook calls opt into reject, skip, or queue semantics with documented retry behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest adjacent product/security-boundary history for session lifecycle and compatibility policy, even though Vincent owns much of the recent hook code path.
